My main difficulty is that once I'm already in a conversation or trying to work, I just completely lose track of my own thoughts and actions.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of sudden, brief, involuntary movements or vocalizations, such as twitching, grimacing, or making odd sounds, which might be related to your strange actions and disorganization?\n\nPatient: I don't think I make odd sounds or have sudden twitches, but I definitely make strange faces and wave my hands around. It's like these things just happen when I'm on the floor, and I really can't explain why I'm doing them.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me at what age you first started noticing these strange behaviors and if they have been present since childhood, or if they started more recently?\n\nPatient: No, they haven't been around since childhood; this all started pretty recently. I'm 20 years old now, and these problems began about a year ago after I left community college to work full-time. I did fine with social interactions and enjoyed normal hobbies like fishing and woodworking without any issues back then.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where you've had difficulty with coordination or balance, such as stumbling, tripping, or having trouble with fine motor tasks like writing or using tools, in addition to the strange actions and pacing you've mentioned?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had any issues with my balance, stumbling, or using tools and writing.
